A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACON, with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on AppWorld, OfficeBench, and 8-objective QA, including compressor distillation, ablations, and qualitative trajectories.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds WebVoyager results and measured latency, among other efficiency analyses.

M1.justification: Threshold-triggered history/observation compression, contrastive utility optimization, compression refinement, and compressor distillation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is reformatted, and the appendix prompts retain their substantive instructions.

E1.justification: V3 adds WebVoyager training and evaluation using webpage accessibility-tree observations (Appendix C.2, Table 6). This extends the three retained productivity and QA benchmarks to a distinct interactive web-browsing domain.

E2.justification: The original task-performance comparator sets are retained. However, v1's API-cost comparison includes FIFO (Figure 7), which is absent from v3's practical-efficiency comparison (Table 4). The new MEM1 table compares design assumptions rather than measured performance.

E3.justification: V3 excludes cached-input discounts from API-cost calculations that included them in v1. It adds median wall-clock latency measured locally with a Qwen3-14B agent and compressor on one A100, separately from the GPT-4.1-based cost evaluation. WebVoyager introduces a 50-task training and 70-task held-out evaluation protocol; existing benchmark splits and thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds quantified latency overhead and a breakdown of trajectory-collection versus guideline-optimization costs. Existing threshold, optimizer, extra-iteration, combined-compression, distillation, and case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 and acknowledge residual nondeterminism. Existing threshold-plot error bars are retained; v3 introduces no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds WebVoyager results: history ACON achieves 48.6% accuracy versus prompting's 42.9%, and observation ACON achieves 47.1% versus 45.7% (Table 6). Table 4 adds cost and latency outcomes under new settings. Original benchmark tables remain unchanged, but Section 4.4 revises the AppWorld baseline from 26.8% to 25.6% and compressed QA EM from 0.197 to 0.23; these revisions do not establish rerun improvements.

T1.justification: The POMDP assumptions, reward-cost objective, compression equations, distillation loss, and dependency definition are unchanged. Splitting and renumbering equations adds no mathematical substance, and the new convergence caveat supplies no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unchanged. V3 more explicitly claims improved success relative to compression baselines, while its conclusion acknowledges small degradation relative to full context. It also narrows the concluding efficiency emphasis from general cost effectiveness to memory efficiency.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's overhead and model-coverage limitations, v3 discusses deployment outside controlled benchmarks, absent convergence guarantees, and distillation data limitations (Appendix A). It adds task-dependent recommendations for UT versus UTCO and interprets reduced uncached API cost alongside increased latency.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v3 reports availability and provides a repository link. V3 explicitly documents ReAct usage and the single UT-plus-CO round, but removes the reproducibility paragraph naming PyTorch, Transformers, TRL, and vLLM. Most hyperparameters and appendix prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning against jointly trained compression policies through Section 2, Appendix C.3, and Table 7, emphasizing model access and agent/compressor decoupling. MEM1 was already cited, but the comparative discussion is new; additional references include context-folding, AgentFold, MemAgent, and ReSum.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, and the efficiency narrative and conclusion are reframed. Appendix C gains subsections, limitations are reorganized, the ethics statement becomes an impact statement, and the separate reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are removed.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main text and extensively reflows displays and appendices. Figure 1 loses its GPT-4.1-mini panel, Figure 2 is redrawn, and the old API-cost Figure 7 is removed. New Tables 4, 6, and 7 are added; the retained observation-distillation Figure 8 becomes Figure 7.

improvement.justification: WebVoyager evaluation and measured latency strengthen evidence about applicability and practical overhead, while expanded limitations better qualify the claims. The net gain is limited: v3 removes the cache-aware cost comparison, so its new API-cost savings cannot establish improved efficiency under v1's assumptions. The core method and original empirical results remain stable.
